title: How Music Sparks Imagination - Nautilus
gist: An article on the neuroscience of music opens with an anecdote of a study subject spontaneously imagining a vivid narrative of dancing cartoon foxes while listening to Aaron Copland's 1938 'Street in a Frontier Town,' framing songs as closely tied to narrative and language processing in the brain.

insights.claim: Songs are closely linked to narrative and language, meaning listening to instrumental music can spontaneously trigger detailed, story-like mental imagery even without lyrics.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Supports use cases for music in narrative-driven media, advertising, and therapeutic storytelling contexts where music is meant to evoke specific imagined scenes.
insights.quote: Songs are closely linked to narrative and language

insights.claim: In an unnamed study, an anonymous subject listening for the first time to Aaron Copland's 'Street in a Frontier Town' (from the 1938 Billy the Kid Suite) spontaneously imagined a detailed narrative of a family of cartoon foxes dancing in turn to shifts in the melody, illustrating how purely instrumental music can generate structured, story-like imagination.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: A concrete illustrative data point for research or product claims linking instrumental music to narrative cognition (e.g., in music-therapy or media-scoring contexts).
insights.locator: Picture a forest setting, dappled light
